references.text: Direct quote in John 2:17. The psalmist writes: "Zeal for your house will consume me." The disciples remembered this scripture when Jesus cleansed the temple and saw it fulfilled in his actions. The Greek καταφάγεταί με ("will consume me") is taken directly from [ref:Sal 69:10|Psalm 69:10].

The psalmist expresses a similar burning zeal: "My zeal has consumed me, because my enemies have forgotten your words" ([ref:Sal 119:139|Psalm 119:139]). This fervor for God's cause reflects the same attitude Jesus showed in the temple.

Phinehas showed zeal for God and was rewarded for it ([ref:4 Mos 25:11-13|Numbers 25:11-13]). His burning passion for the Lord's honor is an Old Testament parallel to Jesus' zealous action in the temple.
Elijah says: "I have been very jealous for the Lord, the God of hosts" ([ref:1 Kong 19:10|1 Kings 19:10]). Elijah's zeal for God's honor is an important example for Jesus' cleansing of the temple.
God calls his temple "a house of prayer" ([ref:Jes 56:7|Isaiah 56:7]). Jesus' zeal for the temple was connected to its purpose as a holy place for worship, not a marketplace.

The context of the disciples' remembrance: Jesus drove out those who were selling and buying in the temple ([ref:Joh 2:14-16|John 2:14-16]). It was this action that caused the disciples to remember the scripture from [ref:Sal 69:10|Psalm 69:10].

The same pattern as in verse 17: "After he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this" ([ref:Joh 2:22|John 2:22]). The disciples understood Scripture and Jesus' words only afterward.

Here too it is told that the disciples did not understand the words of Scripture about Jesus at first: "His disciples did not understand these things at first" ([ref:Joh 12:16|John 12:16]). A similar pattern where the disciples later connect Scripture to Jesus' deeds.

Paul quotes from the same psalm ([ref:Sal 69:10|Psalm 69:10b]) and applies it to Christ: "For even Christ did not please himself, but as it is written: The insults of those who insult you have fallen on me" ([ref:Rom 15:3|Romans 15:3]). This confirms the early church's messianic interpretation of Psalm 69.
Mark's account of the temple cleansing ([ref:Mark 11:15-17|Mark 11:15-17]) gives further details about Jesus' actions and his quote that the temple should be a house of prayer.
